question: What are the four backs' verified 2026 situations, and can an as-of RB workload panel be built without look-ahead?
hypothesis: Team/role must be read from data, not memory; shift-then-roll gives a leak-free panel
dataset: nflverse player_stats+snap_counts+pbp+schedules 2018-2025; rosters 2024-2026; depth charts; FFC ADP 2026; CBS 2026
variables: snap share, carry share, RB target share, RZ/GL carries and shares, receiving role, implied team total, spread, total
validation: assert-based as-of check: debut rows null; f_carries == mean of prior 8 games to 1e-9
result: Montgomery moved DET->HOU (verified 3 ways); panel built and leak-free
uncertainty: depth chart snapshot dated 2026-03-14, predates the 2026 draft

question: Which workload and efficiency components persist season to season, and do any beat last season's points per game out of sample?
hypothesis: Volume persists, TD rate is noise; stable does not imply useful (QB-lab trap)
sample: 464 player-season transitions, 168 players; 331 OOS test rows; split-half n=383
model: OLS baseline (lagged fp/gm) vs baseline+metric, walk-forward
validation: chronological walk-forward; paired bootstrap on squared-error diff; Benjamini-Hochberg q=0.10
metric: r(t,t+1) with bootstrap CI; OOS RMSE gain
result: carries/gm r=0.772; rush TD rate r=0.267 and split-half r=0.172; ZERO metrics survive BH; best gain 0.031 RMSE (0.9%)
effect_size: volume r~0.75, efficiency r~0.0-0.32; high-TD group 0.0454 -> 0.0335 vs league 0.0317
uncertainty: 464 pairs over 7 season pairs; >=8 game filter conditions on survival
oos_result: no metric beats the lagged-points baseline after multiple-testing correction
next_step: model the role distribution, not a point projection

question: What workload distribution does each back face, from comparable historical situations?
hypothesis: A back with a more positively skewed workload distribution than consensus assumes is the edge
dataset: pre-season situation vectors 2019-2025 + FFC ADP history + roster competition
sample: k=30 comparables per target, pool restricted to earlier outcome seasons
variables: prior role, prior games, experience, ADP rank, competition draft capital and prior touches, team change
model: weighted standardised nearest neighbours; weights fixed a priori, not tuned
validation: outcomes joined only after selection; pool strictly earlier seasons; k swept 15-60
metric: role-band probabilities with Wilson intervals; p20/p50/p80 of comparable outcomes
result: P(bellcow): Judkins .47, Swift .43, Pollard .33, Montgomery .07. Skew: Montgomery 1.04, Judkins 0.86, Swift 0.69, Pollard 0.58
effect_size: Montgomery median comparable finish ~RB40 vs market price RB24
uncertainty: 30 comparables; every band probability carries roughly +/-0.17
oos_result: ordering unchanged for every k in 15,20,30,45,60

question: What is each back's full season outcome distribution, and who has the best floor vs the best risk-adjusted ceiling?
hypothesis: Floor and ceiling leaders may be different players; the ranking must survive alternative metrics
dataset: RB-003 comparables + historical RB-game pool matched on season role level
variables: role ratio, games played, per-game FP drawn from role-matched historical games, sampled finish thresholds
validation: measured convergence (5 seeds x 6 sizes); walk-forward coverage backtest; 200-rep comparable bootstrap; 3 role-transfer specs; 6 risk metrics
result: Median: Judkins 185, Swift 160, Pollard 148, Montgomery 79. P(bust): .31/.42/.50/.84. Judkins ranks 1st on all 6 metrics
effect_size: Judkins-Montgomery gap 106 pts (~2 MAE); Judkins-Swift gap 25 pts (inside 1 MAE)
uncertainty: median 95% CI Judkins [155,211] Swift [130,185]; P(Judkins>Swift)=0.89, P(Swift>Pollard)=0.79
oos_result: p25-p75 coverage 0.496 (nominal .50), median unbiased (.489); p10-p90 coverage 0.755 vs .80 so tails ~5pp thin; MAE 57.4 vs 58.7 for a naive ADP curve
critic_verdict: KEEP with ceiling: distributions calibrated, point estimates no sharper than ADP
next_step: only the Montgomery separation is defensible; Judkins over Swift is an 89% lean
